chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from 'Asim ibn Humayd from Abi Basir said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The people ate the meat of their beasts on the day of Khaybar, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered them to cover their pots and forbade them from doing that, but He did not declare it forbidden.'

key_terms.لَمْ يُحَرِّمْهَا: He did not forbid it (declare it haram)

ai.seo_question: Did the Prophet Muhammad declare the meat of pack animals haram during the Battle of Khaybar?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies the legal status of eating the meat of pack animals (dhawa'ib) by distinguishing between temporary prohibition (haram) and mere dislike or advisability (makruh). It highlights that the Prophet’s command to cover the pots was to mitigate the strong odor for the community rather than to declare the meat ritually impure or forbidden, a nuance crucial for Shia jurists in deriving rulings on animal consumption.
